booklet.title: The server application _server: what it is for, what it answers, how to configure it
booklet.author: Giovanni Porcari

purpose.p: Every kajenn server carries one management application, _server (class ServerApplication, package kajenn.server_app). It is the system surface of the server: the login surface for humans, the management of users, credentials, tasks and databases, the monitor, the credential check that channels call, and three site documents (security.txt, robots.txt, favicon.ico).

This booklet states what _server does today on develop: why it exists, every route it answers and who may call it, every recipe word that configures it, how other code extends it, who uses it, and where its browser interface lives. Every fact carries its source.

list.item: For login and user management: an authentication().users(...) store in the recipe.
For OIDC: server(external_url=...) in the recipe.

step.title: Why it exists
step.p: kajenn keeps everything that asks a human for a user and a password out of the core. The core authenticates presented credentials through kajenn.auth and does not import kajenn.server_app; _server is the application that owns the login surface and the management routes, mounted like any other application.
step.fact: The package is the system surface a server exposes under /_server. It holds what asks a human for a user and a password; import kajenn loads none of it.
ServerApplication extends OpenApiApplication, which extends RoutedApplication: its routes are ordinary routes with an OpenAPI description at /_server/_meta/schema_json.
code and mount are both _server, fixed on the class: PasswordMethod names /_server/login as its form action.

step.title: Know when it is mounted
step.p: A server always has _server. The recipe never declares it: it only customises it.

list.item: No application of code _server in the recipe or the kwargs → the server appends a default ServerApplication().
application(code="_server") without app_class → ServerApplication with the words written under it.
application(code="_server", app_class=MyServerApp) → accepted only when MyServerApp subclasses ServerApplication; otherwise the server refuses to build.
The dedicated process of an application declared with spawner="subprocess" mounts no _server: it hosts that application alone.

step.fact: When the process has no role and no application has code _server, a default ServerApplication() is appended to the applications.
An app_class on code _server that is not a ServerApplication subclass raises ValueError naming the class.
A bare server, a recipe naming nothing and a recipe customising _server all mount it; the dedicated process of a spawned application mounts none.

step.title: Know what it answers and who may call it
step.p: Access is decided per route by its auth_rule: no identity answers 401, an identity without the tag answers 403. A route with an openapi_method refuses other methods with 405; a route without one answers every method.

row.cell: /_server/ (index), login, logout, login_methods, _meta/*, OIDC start and callback, the three well-known documents

section.title: The application itself

row.cell: Descriptor: {title, sections}, the attached section names.

identity, password. Checks the lockout, verifies the password against the user store, attaches an Avatar to the current session. Answers {session_id, identity, tags}, or {error} with remaining_attempts for a known identity. Without a user store: "Login is not available".
{methods: [...]}: one descriptor per registered login method (id, kind, label, action), so a front-end draws the login screen without knowing the configuration.
OpenAPI 3.1 document, Swagger UI, HTML index (from OpenApiApplication).

section.fact: index answers the title and the sorted section names.
login is POST, takes identity and password, and attaches the avatar to the current session; the session id does not change.
logout deletes the session it is given.
login_methods is public by design: it lists the descriptors of the registered methods.

section.title: auth: credential check for channels

row.cell: credential, channel. Verifies a presented credential through AuthCore; answers {identity, tags, data, valid_until}. It is the default authentication_route of every channel.
Drops a credential from the caches of every process.
Starts the OIDC authorization code flow with PKCE; 302 to the provider.
Checks the state, exchanges the code, verifies the id_token, attaches the avatar; 302 to the safe next path.

section.fact: authenticate and forget_credential answer 403 to an HTTP caller: only the KajennBus reaches them.
OIDC start stores state, PKCE verifier and the safe next in the session and redirects to the provider; callback (line 207) completes the login.

section.title: users (SUPERADMIN)

row.cell: Every user record without its password hash.
New user: password and confirmation, metadata, tags; the scrypt hash is computed on the server.
Merges metadata into an existing record; the hash is untouched.

section.fact: The CRUD answers 401 anonymous and 403 without SUPERADMIN; without a store every route answers {"error": "User management is not available"}.

section.title: tokens (SUPERADMIN)

row.cell: Every API key record without its secret hash.
label, tags, expires_at. Answers the key gak_... once only.
By key_id; both empty the credential cache in every process.
sub, tags, expires_in. Signs with the first HS* verifier of the recipe.

section.fact: API keys and JWT minting answer 401 anonymous and 403 without SUPERADMIN.

section.title: tasks (SUPERADMIN)

row.cell: A schedule: code, kind, spec, task_name, kwargs, enabled; the next run is computed.
The log of a task by name, with a limit.
Queued and running tasks, by owner or status; progress and result by task_id.

section.fact: Every route is SUPERADMIN; a server with tasks disabled answers {"error": "Tasks are disabled"} with status 200.

section.title: monitor (SERVER_ADMIN)

row.cell: {server, apps}: host, configured port, pid, application and section names; per application its app_snapshot.
Per application its panel descriptor, with the URL of its panel module.
The panel ES module an application provides, or 404.

section.fact: The base app_snapshot is {class, code, mount}; no application in src/ extends it, and no class defines panel_source.

section.title: databases (SERVER_ADMIN)

row.cell: Every database: name, owner, handler class, capabilities.

section.fact: An unknown database answers 404; a handler without the capability answers 422.

section.title: Well-known documents

row.cell: static/favicon.ico exists in the site home

section.p: The three documents are defaults (default_well_known): an application that declares one of these paths in its well_known answers it instead, for example a favicon per host.
section.fact: active_default_well_known builds and validates the two documents and drops every path whose word or file is absent; the full mechanism is in docs/guides/hidden-paths.md.
An application declaring /favicon.ico answers it even when static/favicon.ico exists.

step.title: Configure it
step.p: The words of _server are written under its application element. The recipe customises it; it never has to declare it.

example.title: A recipe customising _server
example.code: server_app = apps.application(code="_server") server_app.login(max_attempts=3, backoff=10) server_app.oidc().provider( code="corp", issuer="https://idp.example.com", client_id="corp-client", client_secret=EnvResolver("CORP_OIDC_SECRET"), ) server_app.security_txt(contact="mailto:security@example.com", expires="2027-06-30T00:00:00Z") robots = server_app.robots(sitemaps="https://example.com/sitemap.xml") robots.agent(user_agent="*", disallow="/admin/")

row.cell: Lockout after consecutive failures; the window doubles at each further failure.
code (required, the collection key), issuer, client_id, client_secret (a resolver; optional for a public client), scopes="openid email profile", identity_claim="email", tags
One login method per provider, mounted at /_server/auth/oidc:<code>/.
contact, expires (required); encryption, acknowledgments, preferred_languages, canonical, policy, hiring
sitemaps; per agent user_agent="*", allow, disallow
The user store behind login and users/*.
The API key store behind tokens/*.
Required with any OIDC provider: the server refuses to boot without it.
The folder whose static/favicon.ico is served.

step.fact: The lock window is backoff * 2 ** (failed - max_attempts) seconds from the last failure; refused attempts while locked do not count, an unknown identity has no counter, a success resets it.
A recipe with an OIDC provider and no external_url is refused at boot.
The login and oidc words of a recipe reach the instance; client_secret goes through the read stack.

step.title: Extend it
step.p: Another package adds routes to _server by attaching a section, and adds a login method by registering it. Both are public methods of ServerApplication.

row.cell: Mounts a RoutingClass at /_server/<name>/ and lists it in sections and in the index.
Adds a login method (kind form, redirect or ceremony); a duplicate id raises ValueError.
The auth section, created on first need.
app_snapshot, app_panel, panel_source on a section
A section declaring them appears in the monitor as _server/<name>.
Replaces the whole application with a subclass.

step.fact: attach_section(section, name) adds the branch and records the section.
register_auth_method registers on the auth section.
A section attached with attach_section answers under /_server/<name>/.

step.title: Know who uses it

row.cell: Every channel of the server (REST, MCP, WSX, KajennBus)
auth/authenticate, to turn a presented credential into an identity.
A spawned application in its dedicated process
The parent's _server: it mounts none of its own.
Login (password or OIDC), then the management routes through a GUI.
The REST routes with an API key or a JWT; docs/guides/management.md shows them with curl.
Attaches its inspector section when the inspector is enabled.
Calls login in-process from its admin views.
Health check of the container on GET /_server.

step.fact: kajenn-orchestra attaches InspectorSection under inspector when the inspector is enabled.
The local HTTPS container checks its health on /_server.
The kajenn command line has no command that calls /_server; kajenn db runs the migrations in-process.

step.title: Find its browser interface
step.p: The browser interface of _server is not in kajenn. It lives in the repository kajenn-org/kajenn-serverapp-gui, today a placeholder holding the first version, built with gramlot and imported from a kajenn working tree. kajenn does not depend on gramlot.
The accepted proposal channels-meta-and-server-gui fixes the shape the GUI takes:

list.item: The recipe enables it with gui(gui_class=...); without the element there is no GUI and the core never names the package.
ServerApplication builds gui_class(self) and passes every request on ui/... to it: the URL is /_server/ui/. The component releases its resources in on_shutdown.
The GUI reads and writes only through the REST routes of _server, like any other client.
Extension pages register on the GUI component when it exists; gramlot is an optional extra of the extension.

step.p: The list of what the GUI must cover is in that repository, in xmldocs/proposal/server-gui-scope.xml.

decision.question: When is the GUI component built as the proposal fixes it?

option.title: Not decided here
option.p: The work belongs to kajenn-serverapp-gui and its scope proposal.

rule.why: The recipe customises _server; the server mounts it anyway.
The configuration handler refuses any other class.

rules.rule: Subclass ServerApplication when replacing _server through app_class.

rule.why: The server refuses to boot without it.

rules.rule: Write server(external_url=...) when any OIDC provider is configured.

rule.why: kajenn does not depend on gramlot.

rules.rule: Import a GUI package from kajenn code.

rule.why: The proposal makes REST the only door of the GUI.

rules.rule: Give every GUI need a REST route on _server before building the page.

limits.limit: The logout docstring says POST, but the route declares no method and answers every one; it has no auth_rule and deletes any session id it is given.
The package docstring still says nothing is mounted automatically; the server mounts _server always. tests/server_app/test_config_server_app.py line 15 says the same.
The monitor serves data only: no page. The per-application snapshot holds class, code and mount; pools, requests, websockets and databases are not in it.
With tasks disabled the tasks routes answer an error with status 200, not an error status.
No route reads or edits the effective configuration, the sessions, the logs or the application list with versions: a GUI cannot show them through REST today.
No route of _server declares a channel: the MCP face of the proposal is not there yet.
